key_insight: Near-equilibrium agreement does not guarantee reliable fatigue dynamics: NequIP predicts much more plastic deformation than EAM under cyclic loading.
engineering_relevance: Fatigue simulations using foundational interatomic potentials need validation of driven, rare-event behavior beyond equilibrium benchmarks.
method: Compare EAM and foundational NequIP potentials on near-equilibrium properties.
Apply fatigue cycling to a nanoscale flaw modeled after a classical Griffith crack.
evidence_signal: Both potentials closely match reference data for many near-equilibrium properties, but NequIP predicts an intrinsic stacking fault energy about sevenfold lower than EAM, with the largest post-loading energy differences occurring beyond thermally accessible energies.
watch_item: Without direct experimental validation of fatigue behavior, the comparison is diagnostic rather than definitive; memory-related crashes and silent extrapolation also warrant monitoring.
paper_title: Emergent Fatigue Dynamics from Foundational Interatomic Potentials
